component.name: Shizumu
component.summary: write · pin · trail · sink. a private thinking space.
écrire · épingler · suivre · déposer. espace d'écriture privé.

description.p: Shizumu is a private thinking space built on four verbs. You write to think, you pin what matters, you trail what continues, and the rest sinks. The volume of writing is not the artifact; what you pin is. No tags, no folders, no templates. The calm of opening the app and not facing a pile.

Pages flow into a daily memory you can scroll back through and search by content. Pins lift the lines that matter out of the daily stream: checklists, references, anything you want close at hand. Trails group writing that belongs together (a project, a book, an ongoing thread of thought) without forcing you to design a structure first. Continuous trails are the one intentional exception: when a single thread should genuinely keep growing, you choose to trail it.

Local-first by design. Everything stays on your device, in a SQLite database you can open with any compatible tool. Optional end-to-end encryption keeps your words readable only by you. No account, no analytics. Your writing remains yours.

Shizumu fits the writer who keeps a daily log, the developer with one running notebook per project, the student capturing reading notes, and anyone who wants a private place to write to think without learning a tagging system first.

Shizumu est un espace d'écriture privé construit sur quatre verbes. Vous écrivez pour penser, vous épinglez ce qui compte, vous suivez ce qui continue, et le reste se dépose. Le volume d'écriture n'est pas l'objet ; ce que vous épinglez l'est. Aucun tag, aucun dossier, aucun gabarit. Le calme d'ouvrir l'application sans faire face à une pile.

Les pages s'écoulent dans une mémoire quotidienne que vous pouvez parcourir et rechercher par contenu. Les épingles soulèvent les lignes qui comptent hors du flux : listes, références, tout ce que vous voulez garder à portée. Les pistes regroupent les écrits qui vont ensemble (un projet, un livre, un fil de pensée en cours) sans imposer de structure préalable. Les pistes continues sont l'exception intentionnelle : quand un seul fil doit vraiment continuer à grandir, vous choisissez de le suivre.

Local d'abord, par conception. Tout reste sur votre appareil, dans une base SQLite que vous pouvez ouvrir avec n'importe quel outil compatible. Le chiffrement de bout en bout, optionnel, garde vos mots lisibles uniquement par vous. Pas de compte, pas d'analytique. Vos écrits vous appartiennent.

Shizumu convient à l'auteur qui tient un journal, au développeur avec un carnet par projet, à l'étudiant qui prend des notes de lecture, et à quiconque cherche un endroit privé pour penser en écrivant, sans devoir apprendre un système de tags d'abord.

description.p: Open beta, and sync arrives. Your writing syncs between your devices end to end encrypted, and the relay that passes it never holds your keys, so it only ever sees ciphertext. Run that relay on your own server, free and unlimited under the AGPL, or use the hosted one: two devices and a gigabyte of attachments, permanently free. Writing itself is never metered on any tier.
Android and Windows join Linux as first builds. Both are honestly labelled: beta means rough edges remain, and it means we would like you to find them.

Both spaces are quieter. Less chrome across the page and memory, and a long pass through the accumulated bug list: the editor settles, the Windows installer settles, and the phone stops putting its controls on top of the words. On a phone the block toolbar keeps the keyboard up when you use it, so pinning a line no longer takes several attempts.

Pinning works on a fresh install. A first-launch database bug dropped a column the pin queries needed, so the pin button did nothing until the app was relaunched. Injecting a pin now carries its title into the block and stays live, so editing the injected copy edits the pin. A synced attachment shows its real name on other devices instead of a content hash. "what settled" keeps its label when tapped, the block controls are smaller on a phone, and a collapsed image can be reopened.

Turning on sync is one tap. The hosted relay is offered by default and says where your writing goes; running your own is still a choice away, and the writing is encrypted before it leaves the device either way.

An image that cannot load no longer leaves its controls floating over the text beneath it. The file is reported as not on this device instead, which is the honest answer. On a phone the image's sync and remove buttons are visible at rest rather than needing a hover that touch does not have.

Phone fixes. The slash and mention menus fit the screen they are on rather than opening under the status bar with their tails off-screen. An edge swipe moves between pages and no longer creates one — on a single-page day every right swipe used to make a new page. Tapping "what settled" shows what the field is instead of a bare cursor. The app no longer draws under the system bars, so the header is not printed beneath the clock. Overlays inside the editor — the chart builder, the pin prompt — land in the viewport again. Rotating to landscape no longer reads as a keyboard that never closes.

Attachments. A file you attach now syncs between your devices, up to 100 MB where the practical limit used to be about one. The bytes travel alongside the sync log instead of inside it, which is also what makes them removable: turn an attachment's sync off and the copy on the relay goes with it, rather than staying there forever. Files are sealed under your current key, so revoking a device stops it reading attachments added afterwards. A pinned file now survives the page it came from — freeing up space no longer takes it away, and unpinning is what releases the bytes. A pin whose file is not on this device says so instead of doing nothing.

The phone interface is reworked. Block actions no longer cover the block they belong to, the header stops printing today twice, and the shell fits the screen with the keyboard up instead of scrolling itself out of view. Edge swipes move between pages the way the arrow keys do on desktop. Rotating the phone keeps the phone layout rather than falling back to the desktop one. Images and files render as blocks you can resize, preview and collapse, and a pinned image looks like an image rather than a file chip.

Sync. End-to-end encrypted sync between your devices, through a relay you run yourself. A new device joins through a short pairing code; old devices can be revoked. Continuous trails ride on a CRDT (Yjs) so two devices writing into the same trail at the same time converge without losing characters or fighting cursors. Discrete pages travel under HLC ordering. Doc identifiers are encrypted in transit — the relay routes ops without learning which page they belong to. Your recovery phrase and the keys derived from it live in the system keyring (libsecret or kwallet), not in the database, so home-directory access doesn't hand over your sync identity. Settings gain a sync section with pause, resume, force-pull, device list, and op log stats. The engine can be turned off entirely if you prefer to stay fully local. The four verbs hold: write, pin, trail, sink — now across your devices.

Editor polish. Block toolbar reappears on empty boards. Frame titles render reliably. Copy works inside structured blocks. Escape behavior is unified across block types. Markdown paste preserves list and task markers across the round-trip. No surface changes; just less friction while writing.

Tray polish. Close-to-tray now keeps the app alive in the system tray instead of quitting, with a settings toggle to flip the behavior. Tray icon is redrawn at the right bit depth so it stops appearing as a colorless square on some Linux desktops.

shizumu, made flexible. Trails you've already made can be reshaped without touching the writing inside them. Rename, move under another trail, fold into a parent, or delete. A new export sends any trail (or every trail) out as readable markdown, one folder per lineage, so your words are never trapped in the app. Underneath: the block and pin rewrite (pin sync moved to a Rust-side cache hook, same-page edits propagate within one editor frame), unified Alt-arrow movement across blocks and list items, midnight transition handling so the day you wrote on stays the day you wrote on, and a quieter writing surface from the rail-system and list-marker rewrites that landed across the v0.2.x line. The four verbs hold: write, pin, trail, sink.

Stabilization release. Pin reactivity fixes: clicking a pinned item in the panel now scrolls and highlights the corresponding block in the editor; renaming a block updates the pin card label without a reload; editing a pin after moving it to a parent page now reflects in the parent's injected copy. Trail highlight updates the moment "what matters now" is saved, no nav roundtrip. Titled boards (lists, blockquotes) survive Enter on an empty item instead of disappearing. Nested outlines render as a continuation of the parent item rather than as a separate panel inside it. New keyboard tools for blocks: Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the current block past its sibling; Tab and Shift+Tab at the start of a block nest or unnest it under the previous sibling. Slash menu adds matching entries for move up, move down, nest, unnest.

Listing polish. Sharpened description (mentions search and optional end-to-end encryption), expanded keywords for note-taking discovery (notetaking, diary, daily, writer, thoughts, ideas, encrypted, minimal), and a clearer "who this is for" paragraph. No app-behavior changes.

Picker-attach replaces the page. When you pick a continuous trail from an empty scratchpad, the scratchpad is consumed instead of lingering as an extra dot. If you'd typed a focus prompt before picking, that focus carries over to today's day-marker on the trail.

Same-day reopen fix. Closing and reopening the app on the same day no longer drops continuous trails you assigned but didn't write on yet. Today's day-marker is now preserved across boots; only past-day empty markers get cleaned up. The user's active session persists; cross-day cleanup still happens naturally tomorrow.

Rail system rewrite. Continuous trails now appear on today's rail by writing on them, the WhatMattersNow gate no longer blocks the editor, and the rail orders dots by when each one was first touched today (a trail picked first sits to the left of pages created later). Empty per-day markers from days the user assigned a trail but never wrote get cleaned up on next launch, so a "I just wanted to peek at this trail" doesn't leave a phantom day-entry tomorrow. Plus several cumulative reliability fixes from rounds 2-7: keyboard-arrow page-creation, picker-attach data-loss protection, today-orphan boot sweep.

Continuous-trail rail fixes. Pressing the right arrow on a continuous trail's living doc no longer spawns empty today-pages on every press, and the desktop-icon launch on Flathub installs is fixed (the exporter was rewriting the launcher to force x11, which has no socket on Wayland sessions). Use "+" to add a new focus; the arrow walks existing rail dots.

Continuous-trail data-loss fix. Switching trails via the picker, unlinking, or moving to a discrete trail while on a continuous trail's living doc no longer destroys the source trail's history. The picker now navigates between continuous trails without merging, and refuses unsafe moves with a hint.

Continuous-trail navigation fixes. Attaching today's page to an existing continuous trail now lands you on today's section with the "what matters now" gate on the new day's first open (previously the editor opened scrolled to yesterday's content), and the prev/next arrows walk today's focuses correctly when the canonical sits on the rail (the canonical now anchors at the right edge so left-arrow no longer dead-ends).

Continuous-trail fix. Attaching today's page to an existing continuous trail now lands you on today's section, with the "what matters now" gate showing on the new day's first open. Previously the editor opened scrolled to yesterday's content.

Listing polish. Refreshed app icon (denser ripple field), correct primary brand colors, capitalized launcher entry, and a refreshed summary. Bundled the new flathub-ready screenshots highlighting v0.2 features (memory, pins panel, trail nesting, settings).

Pin and font fixes. Pinned blocks containing inline images or links no longer render empty when reopened, and opening a pin without editing no longer overwrites its stored content. The font and size selector now applies consistently across the page, the focus rail, and the pin editor.

Tighter writing canvas. The page column no longer feels narrow at small font sizes (820px floor), and the focus pill and footer hug the viewport more closely so the surface feels less stretched on a wide window.
Fix release that brings the editor source in sync with the v0.2.x feature drop. Slash commands, @ subtrails, and list shortcuts now work in the rpm/deb installs as they always have in development.
Diagnostic build to confirm list-item commands are registering correctly. Removed an unused legacy editor extension.
Fixed slash commands and the @ mention popup not opening on the deb/rpm install. Two editor extensions were colliding on the same internal plugin key in production builds; both now register cleanly.

Diagnostic build with developer tools and runtime logging enabled, helping investigate keyboard-shortcut handling on the deb/rpm install. End users will see the same app; logs are written to stderr only when launched from a terminal.

Fixed a typing-hang on KDE Plasma 6 Wayland for the deb/rpm install. The desktop launcher now routes the app through Xwayland so keyboard input reaches the writing surface reliably. Flatpak installs were unaffected.

Mixed list nesting. Bullets, numbered, and tasks freely interleave. Type @ to spawn a child trail without leaving the page. Live font family and size controls. Refreshed app icon. Polish across pins and the writing surface. Now on Flathub.
First Flathub release. Earlier installations are migrated automatically on launch.
New app icon across the window, tray, launcher and dock.
Flatpak packaging fixes and cleaner integration with KDE and GNOME tray icons.
Embed local images in the editor with resize and collapse-to-chip. Pins now follow their source page across trail moves and survive trail deletion.
Trails, pins, and the choice between continuous and discrete writing modes.
Initial release. The writing page and chronological memory view.
